answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making each identity pay its own way: a plume of cheap accounts collapses once every claim requires staked collateral that burns on fraud. Peers run inlet checks over time, so a fake history costs continuous upkeep, while opal pricing ties each new persona to a real fee. Attackers then face a simple arithmetic — one more sockpuppet costs more than it can extract — and honest agents, verified once and reused often, stay cheap.
